self.title: What If Our Starting Assumptions Are Wrong?

detail.title: Foundational Constraints in AI Metareasoning
detail.summary: AI metareasoning is currently bifurcated: established 'resource partition' models focus on computational efficiency, while emerging epistemological frameworks like 'Equity Bias' advocate for making foundational assumptions explicit and contestable. Current LLMs can support the transparency of these assumptions, but autonomous self-correction of foundational premises remains unproven.
detail.reason: Revising the notebook to incorporate the 'Equity Bias' framework provides a clearer pathway to addressing the project's question on assumption identification.

detail.title: Meta-Reasoning and Assumption Correction
detail.question: Can an intelligent system identify a foundational assumption underlying its own reasoning, demonstrate its inadequacy, and develop a better alternative?
detail.reason: The project is now focused on the intersection of epistemic transparency (Equity Bias) and potential automation. The next step is to investigate if existing prompt-engineering or agentic-flow patterns approximate the 'Equity Archaeology' methodology.

detail.title: Foundational Constraints in AI Metareasoning
detail.summary: AI metareasoning has traditionally focused on resource allocation (the partition problem) rather than the active, explicit identification or falsification of its own internal epistemic assumptions. Current LLM research demonstrates emergent problem-solving behaviors, but evidence for the specific, intentional correction of flawed foundational assumptions remains anecdotal or tied to external prompting, rather than an autonomous internal mechanism.
detail.reason: This notebook synthesizes existing metareasoning literature with emerging LLM scaling and emergent-behavior research to address the project question.
